text:
sara: Heads up — support just opened a ticket: customer sees repeated 502s/timeouts hitting hosted inference since the staged release this morning. stack traces show gateway upstream timeouts.
support_maya: Customer report: ~30% of requests return 502, others succeed. They pasted this response body: "error: upstream timeout while proxying to auth-service". request id x-request-id=acme-7732.
eng_ryan: tagging in. Which release tag and which traffic slice did we push?
sara: release tag: release-2026-03-14-482, traffic slice shifted from 10% -> 40% at 09:22 PT.
ops_alex: @eng_ryan I see a deploy spike at 09:20; canary weight ramped with the new header-normalizer middleware enabled.
support_maya: Customer provided a repro curl: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept-Encoding: gzip" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` They tried with and without gzip; both fail intermittently.
eng_ryan: hmm. The header-normalizer change added percent-encoding for non-ASCII header bytes. Might be an edge-case where certain Accept-Encoding combos trigger early connection close in the gateway -> auth-service chain.
ops_tess: I'm seeing increased 502s in the metric dashboards for api-router-prod (region us-west). Error rate jumps exactly at 09:22.
infra-bot: [ALERT] api-router-prod.us-west: 502 spike, 5xx rate 4.8% -> 18.2% over 10m.
eng_ryan: Can we get a full proxy trace for one failing request? Ask support to capture x-request-id and any trace headers.
support_maya: Customer sent request id acme-7732 and x-trace: trace-0a9f. They also attached tcpdump and gateway logs (snippet): ```2026-03-14T09:22:43Z router[pid] WARN upstream timeout id=acme-7732 target=auth-service-1 2.5s```
ops_alex: I can tail router logs for that id. Running: ```kubectl logs -n prod deploy/api-router -c router --since=5m | grep acme-7732```
ops_alex: Found it — router accepted connection, forwarded to auth-service but auth-service didn't ack for ~2.5s then we returned 502. Auth pods show increased cpu latency around that time.
eng_ryan: Could be the header-normalizer introducing an extra CPU cost in auth-service if it's decoding headers on every request. Did we roll a new auth-sidecar config?
sara: Not for auth-service. Only api-router got the middleware. But api-router changes change how headers are forwarded (encoding). Maybe auth-service library chokes on encoded headers and does blocking operation.
eng_ryan: Let's reproduce locally: I'll spin up api-router image with middleware flag and run synthetic traffic against auth-service stub.
eng_ryan: repro steps I ran: ```export ROUTER_IMG=release-2026-03-14-482 && docker run -e ENABLE_HEADER_NORMALIZER=1 $ROUTER_IMG && ab -n 1000 -c 20 -H "Authorization: Bearer foo" http://router.local/v1/generate``` saw 5xx in ~20% of requests, cpu spikes.
ops_tess: Immediate mitigation: scale auth-service pods + increase readiness timeouts? Or cut canary weight.
ops_alex: Initiating quick rollback of the header-normalizer flag on api-router canary. Setting staged config weight back to 10%. Command: ```redwoodctl rollout set-weight api-router canary 10```
ops_alex: Doing it now.
infra-bot: [ACTION] rollout set-weight api-router canary -> 10 by ops_alex at 09:35
eng_ryan: Also let's add a temporary circuit in api-router to treat header decoding failures as non-blocking (fallback). I'll open a PR but don't want to roll it now.
support_maya: Escalated to customer: we scaled back the canary and are investigating. asked them to test again in 10m.
ops_tess: After weight rollback, 5xx rate dropped to 3.1% in 5m window.
infra-bot: [RECOVERY] api-router-prod.us-west: 5xx rate decreased to 3.1% at 09:42.
support_maya: Customer confirms their requests are succeeding now (reported 200s). :white_check_mark:
eng_ryan: Root cause likely header-normalizer + specific Accept-Encoding combos causing router->auth blocking. Next steps: full postmortem, add unit tests for header transforms in auth client, and make the middleware opt-in per-tenant.
sara: Agreed. @eng_ryan please drive the postmortem. ops, add a rollback play entry to the runbook for header-transform toggles.
ops_alex: Will update runbook and add a quick rollback runbook step (one-liner).
eng_ryan: Opening postmortem draft now with repro commands/log snippets.
sara: Great. Thanks everyone for fast response. Closing loop when postmortem is up.
ops_tess: Logging incident in tracker: INC-2026-0031.
eng_ryan: PR to add defensive parsing + test: #4021
support_maya: Noted; I'll follow up with customer once postmortem link is ready.
sara: :thumbsup:
